info.title: OpenAsy Endpoints API
info.summary: Every laptop and workstation, encrypted, updated and locked, read by osquery on each device.
info.description:
Every screen of Endpoints uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003) and takes a session or an API token. The two `/api/v1/osquery` operations are osquery's own protocol: osquery calls them with its enrolment secret or node key in the body, and they answer in osquery's shape. Endpoints never sends a device a query; the queries are in the pack on the device (ADR 0065).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.summary: Enrol a device (osquery's TLS enroll plugin)
post.description: Called by osquery, not by people: `--enroll_tls_endpoint`. The enrolment secret is in the body, as osquery sends it. A refused enrolment is answered 200 with `node_invalid: true`, as osquery expects, and osquery tries again later. A hardware UUID that is enrolled already is refused until an admin allows it to enrol again.

Called by osquery, not by people: `--logger_tls_endpoint`, gzipped with `--logger_tls_compress`. The node key is in the body. Snapshots of the pack's queries are kept; other results and status logs are dropped. An unknown node key is answered with `node_invalid: true`, which makes osquery enrol again. At most 16 MiB unpacked.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Every device that enrolled, with its posture and checks.
Needs the viewer role. With each check and its exception, the local accounts and how much software it has.

put.description: Needs the editor role. The owner is free text, such as an email address; null or an empty string clears it.

delete.description: Needs the admin role. Its node key stops working and what it reported is deleted. osquery on it enrols again as a new device while its secret is valid.

post.description: Needs the admin role. For a device whose osquery lost its node key, such as after a reinstall: the same hardware UUID may enrol once within 7 days, and its old node key stops working then.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Each application by name, with its versions, the newest first, and how many devices are not on the newest any device has. The 1,000 on most devices; total counts all.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Each check's counts, postures by platform, and every failing check on every device, blocked first.

put.description: Needs the admin role. Fields left out keep their value. Every device is checked again against what it already reported; a check that starts failing now starts its grace period now.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Active ones first.

post.description: Needs the admin role. A failing check on one device counts as passing until it ends, at most a year on. One active exception per device and check.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Never the secret itself: a fingerprint, its expiry and how many devices enrolled with it.

post.description: Needs the admin role. The secret is in this answer only. Many devices may enrol with it until it expires, 90 days on unless set.
Needs the admin role. No new device enrols with it. Devices that enrolled with it keep their own node keys.

get.summary: What to put on a device
get.description: Needs the viewer role. The osquery flags and the steps for each platform, and the query pack. The enrolment secret is not in it.
Needs the viewer role. Every enrolment, refused enrolment, change to devices, the policy, exceptions and secrets, and sign-in, newest first. Rows are never changed or removed.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Endpoints runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Endpoints origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings, API tokens (`oa_endpoints_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Endpoints is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

host_details.description: osquery's system_info, os_version, osquery_info and platform_info.

data.description: Result logs: snapshots of the pack's queries, with name, snapshot, unixTime and decorations.

node_key.description: After enrolment: the device's own key, sent with every result.

graceEndsAt.description: When the device becomes non-compliant for it; null when it blocks at once.

blocked.description: It counts against the device now: the check blocks, or its grace period ended.

uuid.description: The hardware UUID osquery reports; a device is found again by it.

platform.description: osquery's os_version.platform, such as darwin, windows, ubuntu or debian.

packVersion.description: The version of the query pack it runs; empty until its first result.

stale.description: It has not checked in within the policy's stale days.

reenrollUntil.description: Until when it may enrol again, when an admin allowed it.

posture.description: pending while osquery has not answered a check that applies, and nothing fails.

since.description: Since when it has this status.

software.description: How many applications and packages it has.

notOnNewest.description: Devices without the newest version any device has. A sign, not an advisory.

graceDays.description: How long a failing check with onFailure grace leaves a device at risk.

linux.description: By osquery's os_version.platform: {"ubuntu": "22.04"}. A distribution not named is not checked.

checks.description: Some checks, each with enabled and onFailure, both optional.

graceDays.description: How long a failing check with onFailure grace leaves a device at risk.

linux.description: By osquery's os_version.platform: {"ubuntu": "22.04"}. A distribution not named is not checked.

secret.description: Shown this once. Put it in the enroll_secret file on each device.

https.description: false when ENDPOINTS_PUBLIC_URL is not https://: osquery connects only over TLS.

pack.description: osquery.conf, the query pack: the same on every device.
